definition: A driving-desk controller used to request traction and/or braking; this teaching layout has EB, B3, B2, B1, N, P1, P2 and P3 positions.
Propulsive effort generated by a train’s traction system to move or accelerate the vehicle.
Movement without an active power request from the driving controller.
A defined, often mechanically indexed position of a driving control lever.
A controller setting that requests neither active traction nor service braking from a combined handle.
A train control for choosing the intended direction of travel where the vehicle design provides such a control.
A safety system intended to check that the driver remains responsive and to initiate a prescribed response if required acknowledgements are not made.
